## Chef's Note

This frozen dessert mimics the exact flavor profile of our [Key Lime Pie](/mise/recipes/key-lime-pie). The secret to a smooth, professional churn is the condensed milk: the sugar and fats act as a powerful stabilizer, preventing the formation of large ice crystals and ensuring a silky texture. We use a two-part graham cracker approach - stir half into the churn and reserve the other half for topping just before serving. This ensures you have both soft, cake-like bits and shatteringly crisp pieces.

## Directions

1.  **The Base:** In a large bowl, whisk together the condensed milk, key lime juice, 2% milk, cream, and salt until perfectly smooth.
2.  **The Churn:** Pour the mixture into your ice cream maker. Churn according to the manufacturer's instructions (usually 20-25 minutes).
3.  **The Crunch:** During the last 2 minutes of churning, add 1/3 cup of the coarsely crushed graham crackers.
4.  **The Finish:** Transfer the soft-serve consistency ice cream to a chilled, freezer-safe container. Cover and freeze for **at least 4 hours** (ideally overnight) to firm up.
5.  **Serve:** Scoop into bowls. Top with the remaining reserved graham cracker crumbs and a fresh lime wedge for the mandatory **Acid Balance**.

## Chef's Note

Sweetened condensed milk gives this [Key lime pie](/mise/recipes/key-lime-pie)-inspired ice cream sweetness and body, while the full cream and milk round out the lime. Fold half the coarsely crushed graham crackers into the churned ice cream and keep half dry for serving: the mix-ins soften, while the topping stays crisp.

## Directions

1. **Whisk and chill the base:** Whisk fat-free sweetened condensed milk, Key lime juice, 2% milk, heavy whipping cream, and sea salt in a bowl until smooth. Use pasteurized milk and cream. Cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below until thoroughly cold; keep the base refrigerated until churning. Prepare the ice-cream machine’s freezer bowl or compressor according to its manual before starting.
2. **Churn within the machine limit:** Pour the cold base into the prepared ice-cream maker, staying below its maximum working fill so there is room as it churns. Churn according to the machine instructions until thick and soft-serve-like. If the batch exceeds capacity, use complete smaller churns and keep the waiting base refrigerated; a freezer bowl may need to be fully refrozen between batches.
3. **Fold in half the crumbs:** Use 1/2 of the quarter-sheet graham cracker pieces for this stage. Divide the complete crushed-cracker supply into equal halves; keep the other half dry for serving. Fold this half gently into the churned ice cream after churning, or add near the end only if the machine manual permits mix-ins. Use the complete listed cracker supply for these two equal portions.
4. **Freeze until firm:** Transfer to a chilled freezer-safe container with room for the complete batch. Cover closely and freeze at 0°F / −18°C until firm enough to scoop, planning at least 4 hours and preferably overnight. Container depth, freezer temperature and batch size affect firming; four hours is a starting plan rather than a guarantee.
5. **Add the crisp topping:** Use 1/2 of the quarter-sheet graham cracker pieces and Key lime wedges (if using). Divide the remaining dry half of the crumbs among the servings and add lime wedges if desired. Soften the ice cream only as needed for scooping, and promptly return the rest to the freezer.

## Chef's Note

Roasted corn, rendered bacon fat and smoked paprika give this creamy chowder layered sweetness and smoke. Cook the potatoes until tender before adding shrimp, then finish the shrimp gently and stir in lime off the heat. Robert Irvine’s separate roux-and-cream version below keeps its full vegetables, cream and garnishes.

## Directions

1. **Roast the corn:** Preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Toss corn kernels, neutral vegetable oil, and salt and black pepper on a rimmed sheet pan and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 15 minutes, stirring as needed, until fragrant with browned edges, without blackening. Use more pans or roasting loads at larger scales. Begin the pot stages while the corn roasts.
2. **Render the bacon:** Use slices of bacon in a roomy heavy-bottomed soup pot over medium heat. Cook until crisp, stirring, then transfer the bacon bits to a plate and leave all rendered fat in the pot.
3. **Soften the onion:** Add red onion to the bacon fat and cook about 5 minutes until softened without burning.
4. **Add garlic and paprika:** Stir in garlic cloves and smoked paprika and cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant; lower the heat if they catch.
5. **Cook the potatoes:** Add Red Bliss potatoes and chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for about 15–20 minutes, until a fork passes easily through the potato pieces. Stir occasionally so the bottom stays clear; the pot needs headroom above the full liquids and vegetables.
6. **Thicken while keeping texture:** Stir in heavy cream and all the roasted corn. Take the pot safely off the heat. With a hot-liquid-rated immersion blender, keep the blade guard submerged, pulse briefly and stop the motor before lifting it; begin with 3–4 short pulses and leave recognizable corn and potato pieces. Return to low heat and bring to a gentle simmer.
7. **Cook the shrimp completely:** Stir in all raw shrimp. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
8. **Finish with lime and bacon:** Turn off the heat and stir in fresh lime juice and all reserved bacon bits. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve promptly while the shrimp remain tender.

## Cooking Notes

For a fresh count-based version of the six-portion chowder, use all kernels from 4 ears instead of the measured 3 cups and scale that ear count with the planned portions; ear size makes its corn density variable. Keep all other main ingredients and method stages the same. The Robert Irvine version below uses its own measured 2 cups corn and eight-portion formula; these are separate complete choices.

## Robert Irvine’s roux-and-cream version

This complete alternative makes 8 planned portions. Choose its ingredient list and method together; at another yield, scale the entire list proportionally. The oil is one ¼ cup total, divided equally between roasting and the pot. The roux, cream, bacon, peppers and garnishes all belong to this version.

- 1 lime, juice and squeezed rind for shrimp marinade; marinade/rind discarded
- 1 lb raw baby shrimp, shelled, deveined and thawed under refrigeration if frozen
- 2 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed frozen and drained; do not use canned corn
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil, one total, divided equally between corn roasting and the pot
- 1/2 cup raw bacon, chopped
- 1 red onion, diced
- 1/2 cup celery, finely diced
- 1 green bell pepper, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 6 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 cups heavy cream
- 6 cups chicken stock
- 1/2 lb Red Bliss potatoes, diced into similar small pieces
- 3 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley leaves, chopped
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
- 1 bunch of scallions, chopped
- oyster crackers, as an accompaniment

1. **Chill the lime-marinated shrimp:** Use lime and raw baby shrimp: squeeze the lime over the raw shrimp, add the squeezed rind, stir, cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below while preparing the chowder, for no longer than 1 hour. At large scales, start marinating close enough to the shrimp-cooking stage to keep within that hour; keep all waiting raw shrimp refrigerated.
2. **Roast the corn with half the oil:** Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Coat corn kernels and 1/2 of the vegetable oil on a rimmed baking sheet and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 5–10 minutes until fragrant and lightly colored; do not require blackening. Keep the remaining half of the listed oil for the pot.
3. **Cook the bacon with the remaining oil:** Heat 1/2 of the vegetable oil and raw bacon in a heavy-bottomed soup pot over low heat until the bacon is crisp, stirring. Keep all the bacon and fat in the pot.
4. **Soften onion and celery:** Add red onion and celery and cook about 5 minutes without browning.
5. **Add peppers, garlic and corn:** Add green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and garlic cloves and all the roasted corn. Cook another 5 minutes over low heat, stirring without letting the garlic burn.
6. **Cook the flour gently:** Stir in all-purpose flour and cook 6–8 minutes over low heat, stirring so the flour coats the vegetables and does not stick or scorch.
7. **Simmer the creamy base:** Use heavy cream, chicken stock, and Red Bliss potatoes. Stir in the stock gradually to disperse the flour, then add all the cream and potatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 20 minutes, stirring the bottom, until the potatoes are fork-tender. Avoid a hard boil or stuck roux; use a pot with ample working headroom.
8. **Drain and heat the shrimp:** Remove shrimp from the marinade and discard the liquid and lime rind. Add all shrimp with fresh lime juice, fresh parsley leaves, and cayenne pepper to the gently simmering chowder. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
9. **Garnish with scallions:** Spoon the chowder into bowls and add bunch of scallions and oyster crackers. Serve promptly; all the cream, oil, bacon and vegetables belong to this complete version.

Allow roughly 75–120 minutes elapsed with 45–60 minutes active work, starting with thawed shrimp and including up to 1 hour refrigerated marinating. Roast corn and build the pot base while shrimp marinate, keeping within that hour. Use the same shrimp endpoint, cold-storage and reheating guidance as above.

## Chef's Note

Roasted corn, rendered bacon fat and smoked paprika give this creamy chowder layered sweetness and smoke. Cook the potatoes until tender before adding shrimp, then finish the shrimp gently and stir in lime off the heat. Robert Irvine’s separate roux-and-cream version below keeps its full vegetables, cream and garnishes.

## Directions

1. **Roast the corn:** Preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Toss corn kernels, neutral vegetable oil, and salt and black pepper on a rimmed sheet pan and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 15 minutes, stirring as needed, until fragrant with browned edges, without blackening. Use more pans or roasting loads at larger scales. Begin the pot stages while the corn roasts.
2. **Render the bacon:** Use slices of bacon in a roomy heavy-bottomed soup pot over medium heat. Cook until crisp, stirring, then transfer the bacon bits to a plate and leave all rendered fat in the pot.
3. **Soften the onion:** Add red onion to the bacon fat and cook about 5 minutes until softened without burning.
4. **Add garlic and paprika:** Stir in garlic cloves and smoked paprika and cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant; lower the heat if they catch.
5. **Cook the potatoes:** Add Red Bliss potatoes and chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for about 15–20 minutes, until a fork passes easily through the potato pieces. Stir occasionally so the bottom stays clear; the pot needs headroom above the full liquids and vegetables.
6. **Thicken while keeping texture:** Stir in heavy cream and all the roasted corn. Take the pot safely off the heat. With a hot-liquid-rated immersion blender, keep the blade guard submerged, pulse briefly and stop the motor before lifting it; begin with 3–4 short pulses and leave recognizable corn and potato pieces. Return to low heat and bring to a gentle simmer.
7. **Cook the shrimp completely:** Stir in all raw shrimp. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
8. **Finish with lime and bacon:** Turn off the heat and stir in fresh lime juice and all reserved bacon bits. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve promptly while the shrimp remain tender.

## Cooking Notes

For a fresh count-based version of the six-portion chowder, use all kernels from 4 ears instead of the measured 3 cups and scale that ear count with the planned portions; ear size makes its corn density variable. Keep all other main ingredients and method stages the same. The Robert Irvine version below uses its own measured 2 cups corn and eight-portion formula; these are separate complete choices.

## Robert Irvine’s roux-and-cream version

This complete alternative makes 8 planned portions. Choose its ingredient list and method together; at another yield, scale the entire list proportionally. The oil is one ¼ cup total, divided equally between roasting and the pot. The roux, cream, bacon, peppers and garnishes all belong to this version.

- 1 lime, juice and squeezed rind for shrimp marinade; marinade/rind discarded
- 1 lb raw baby shrimp, shelled, deveined and thawed under refrigeration if frozen
- 2 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed frozen and drained; do not use canned corn
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil, one total, divided equally between corn roasting and the pot
- 1/2 cup raw bacon, chopped
- 1 red onion, diced
- 1/2 cup celery, finely diced
- 1 green bell pepper, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 6 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 cups heavy cream
- 6 cups chicken stock
- 1/2 lb Red Bliss potatoes, diced into similar small pieces
- 3 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley leaves, chopped
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
- 1 bunch of scallions, chopped
- oyster crackers, as an accompaniment

1. **Chill the lime-marinated shrimp:** Use lime and raw baby shrimp: squeeze the lime over the raw shrimp, add the squeezed rind, stir, cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below while preparing the chowder, for no longer than 1 hour. At large scales, start marinating close enough to the shrimp-cooking stage to keep within that hour; keep all waiting raw shrimp refrigerated.
2. **Roast the corn with half the oil:** Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Coat corn kernels and 1/2 of the vegetable oil on a rimmed baking sheet and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 5–10 minutes until fragrant and lightly colored; do not require blackening. Keep the remaining half of the listed oil for the pot.
3. **Cook the bacon with the remaining oil:** Heat 1/2 of the vegetable oil and raw bacon in a heavy-bottomed soup pot over low heat until the bacon is crisp, stirring. Keep all the bacon and fat in the pot.
4. **Soften onion and celery:** Add red onion and celery and cook about 5 minutes without browning.
5. **Add peppers, garlic and corn:** Add green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and garlic cloves and all the roasted corn. Cook another 5 minutes over low heat, stirring without letting the garlic burn.
6. **Cook the flour gently:** Stir in all-purpose flour and cook 6–8 minutes over low heat, stirring so the flour coats the vegetables and does not stick or scorch.
7. **Simmer the creamy base:** Use heavy cream, chicken stock, and Red Bliss potatoes. Stir in the stock gradually to disperse the flour, then add all the cream and potatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 20 minutes, stirring the bottom, until the potatoes are fork-tender. Avoid a hard boil or stuck roux; use a pot with ample working headroom.
8. **Drain and heat the shrimp:** Remove shrimp from the marinade and discard the liquid and lime rind. Add all shrimp with fresh lime juice, fresh parsley leaves, and cayenne pepper to the gently simmering chowder. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
9. **Garnish with scallions:** Spoon the chowder into bowls and add bunch of scallions and oyster crackers. Serve promptly; all the cream, oil, bacon and vegetables belong to this complete version.

Allow roughly 75–120 minutes elapsed with 45–60 minutes active work, starting with thawed shrimp and including up to 1 hour refrigerated marinating. Roast corn and build the pot base while shrimp marinate, keeping within that hour. Use the same shrimp endpoint, cold-storage and reheating guidance as above.

## Chef's Note

Sweetened condensed milk gives this [Key lime pie](/mise/recipes/key-lime-pie)-inspired ice cream sweetness and body, while the full cream and milk round out the lime. Fold half the coarsely crushed graham crackers into the churned ice cream and keep half dry for serving: the mix-ins soften, while the topping stays crisp.

## Directions

1. **Whisk and chill the base:** Whisk fat-free sweetened condensed milk, Key lime juice, 2% milk, heavy whipping cream, and sea salt in a bowl until smooth. Use pasteurized milk and cream. Cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below until thoroughly cold; keep the base refrigerated until churning. Prepare the ice-cream machine’s freezer bowl or compressor according to its manual before starting.
2. **Churn within the machine limit:** Pour the cold base into the prepared ice-cream maker, staying below its maximum working fill so there is room as it churns. Churn according to the machine instructions until thick and soft-serve-like. If the batch exceeds capacity, use complete smaller churns and keep the waiting base refrigerated; a freezer bowl may need to be fully refrozen between batches.
3. **Fold in half the crumbs:** Use 1/2 of the quarter-sheet graham cracker pieces for this stage. Divide the complete crushed-cracker supply into equal halves; keep the other half dry for serving. Fold this half gently into the churned ice cream after churning, or add near the end only if the machine manual permits mix-ins. Use the complete listed cracker supply for these two equal portions.
4. **Freeze until firm:** Transfer to a chilled freezer-safe container with room for the complete batch. Cover closely and freeze at 0°F / −18°C until firm enough to scoop, planning at least 4 hours and preferably overnight. Container depth, freezer temperature and batch size affect firming; four hours is a starting plan rather than a guarantee.
5. **Add the crisp topping:** Use 1/2 of the quarter-sheet graham cracker pieces and Key lime wedges (if using). Divide the remaining dry half of the crumbs among the servings and add lime wedges if desired. Soften the ice cream only as needed for scooping, and promptly return the rest to the freezer.

## Chef's Note

Richard Blais’s risotto-style oats soak overnight in the refrigerator, then cook in all their soaking liquid until creamy with a slight chew. Mashed overripe banana gives body; drained sherry-vinegar raisins supply the sweet-sour finish. Generous Parmesan shavings add savory depth if using, with optional extra brown sugar for serving.

## Directions

1. **Refrigerate the overnight soak:** Combine steel-cut oats and water or chicken stock or broth in a covered bowl. Refrigerate overnight at 40°F / 4°C or below. Keep the covered oats and all soaking liquid cold until ready to cook.
2. **Soak the raisins:** Put golden raisins and sherry vinegar in a small bowl and stir so the vinegar coats the raisins. Let them stand while the oats cook; drain the soaking vinegar before topping.
3. **Bring the oats to a simmer:** Pour the oats and all their soaking liquid into a saucepan with headroom for bubbling. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Add light brown sugar and kosher salt and stir.
4. **Cook by texture:** Stir occasionally, including the bottom, and start checking around 20 minutes. Continue until the oats are tender with a slight chew, without hard centers. Lower the heat if the bottom catches. Use additional hot water only if extended simmering makes the mixture dry before the oats soften; add a small splash at a time, keeping the porridge cohesive.
5. **Fold in the banana:** Add overripe banana and cook about 2 minutes more, stirring until the banana is evenly incorporated and hot throughout.
6. **Drain the raisins and finish:** Drain the soaked raisins and discard the free vinegar. Divide the oats among the listed portions and distribute all the drained raisins among them. Use Parmesan cheese (if using) and light brown sugar (if using): add generous Parmesan shavings if using, and offer the optional extra sugar. Serve promptly.

## Chef's Note

Roasted corn, rendered bacon fat and smoked paprika give this creamy chowder layered sweetness and smoke. Cook the potatoes until tender before adding shrimp, then finish the shrimp gently and stir in lime off the heat. Robert Irvine’s separate roux-and-cream version below keeps its full vegetables, cream and garnishes.

## Directions

1. **Roast the corn:** Preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Toss corn kernels, neutral vegetable oil, and salt and black pepper on a rimmed sheet pan and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 15 minutes, stirring as needed, until fragrant with browned edges, without blackening. Use more pans or roasting loads at larger scales. Begin the pot stages while the corn roasts.
2. **Render the bacon:** Use slices of bacon in a roomy heavy-bottomed soup pot over medium heat. Cook until crisp, stirring, then transfer the bacon bits to a plate and leave all rendered fat in the pot.
3. **Soften the onion:** Add red onion to the bacon fat and cook about 5 minutes until softened without burning.
4. **Add garlic and paprika:** Stir in garlic cloves and smoked paprika and cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant; lower the heat if they catch.
5. **Cook the potatoes:** Add Red Bliss potatoes and chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for about 15–20 minutes, until a fork passes easily through the potato pieces. Stir occasionally so the bottom stays clear; the pot needs headroom above the full liquids and vegetables.
6. **Thicken while keeping texture:** Stir in heavy cream and all the roasted corn. Take the pot safely off the heat. With a hot-liquid-rated immersion blender, keep the blade guard submerged, pulse briefly and stop the motor before lifting it; begin with 3–4 short pulses and leave recognizable corn and potato pieces. Return to low heat and bring to a gentle simmer.
7. **Cook the shrimp completely:** Stir in all raw shrimp. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
8. **Finish with lime and bacon:** Turn off the heat and stir in fresh lime juice and all reserved bacon bits. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve promptly while the shrimp remain tender.

## Cooking Notes

For a fresh count-based version of the six-portion chowder, use all kernels from 4 ears instead of the measured 3 cups and scale that ear count with the planned portions; ear size makes its corn density variable. Keep all other main ingredients and method stages the same. The Robert Irvine version below uses its own measured 2 cups corn and eight-portion formula; these are separate complete choices.

## Robert Irvine’s roux-and-cream version

This complete alternative makes 8 planned portions. Choose its ingredient list and method together; at another yield, scale the entire list proportionally. The oil is one ¼ cup total, divided equally between roasting and the pot. The roux, cream, bacon, peppers and garnishes all belong to this version.

- 1 lime, juice and squeezed rind for shrimp marinade; marinade/rind discarded
- 1 lb raw baby shrimp, shelled, deveined and thawed under refrigeration if frozen
- 2 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed frozen and drained; do not use canned corn
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil, one total, divided equally between corn roasting and the pot
- 1/2 cup raw bacon, chopped
- 1 red onion, diced
- 1/2 cup celery, finely diced
- 1 green bell pepper, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 6 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 cups heavy cream
- 6 cups chicken stock
- 1/2 lb Red Bliss potatoes, diced into similar small pieces
- 3 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley leaves, chopped
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
- 1 bunch of scallions, chopped
- oyster crackers, as an accompaniment

1. **Chill the lime-marinated shrimp:** Use lime and raw baby shrimp: squeeze the lime over the raw shrimp, add the squeezed rind, stir, cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below while preparing the chowder, for no longer than 1 hour. At large scales, start marinating close enough to the shrimp-cooking stage to keep within that hour; keep all waiting raw shrimp refrigerated.
2. **Roast the corn with half the oil:** Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Coat corn kernels and 1/2 of the vegetable oil on a rimmed baking sheet and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 5–10 minutes until fragrant and lightly colored; do not require blackening. Keep the remaining half of the listed oil for the pot.
3. **Cook the bacon with the remaining oil:** Heat 1/2 of the vegetable oil and raw bacon in a heavy-bottomed soup pot over low heat until the bacon is crisp, stirring. Keep all the bacon and fat in the pot.
4. **Soften onion and celery:** Add red onion and celery and cook about 5 minutes without browning.
5. **Add peppers, garlic and corn:** Add green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and garlic cloves and all the roasted corn. Cook another 5 minutes over low heat, stirring without letting the garlic burn.
6. **Cook the flour gently:** Stir in all-purpose flour and cook 6–8 minutes over low heat, stirring so the flour coats the vegetables and does not stick or scorch.
7. **Simmer the creamy base:** Use heavy cream, chicken stock, and Red Bliss potatoes. Stir in the stock gradually to disperse the flour, then add all the cream and potatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 20 minutes, stirring the bottom, until the potatoes are fork-tender. Avoid a hard boil or stuck roux; use a pot with ample working headroom.
8. **Drain and heat the shrimp:** Remove shrimp from the marinade and discard the liquid and lime rind. Add all shrimp with fresh lime juice, fresh parsley leaves, and cayenne pepper to the gently simmering chowder. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
9. **Garnish with scallions:** Spoon the chowder into bowls and add bunch of scallions and oyster crackers. Serve promptly; all the cream, oil, bacon and vegetables belong to this complete version.

Allow roughly 75–120 minutes elapsed with 45–60 minutes active work, starting with thawed shrimp and including up to 1 hour refrigerated marinating. Roast corn and build the pot base while shrimp marinate, keeping within that hour. Use the same shrimp endpoint, cold-storage and reheating guidance as above.

## Chef's Note

Roasted corn, rendered bacon fat and smoked paprika give this creamy chowder layered sweetness and smoke. Cook the potatoes until tender before adding shrimp, then finish the shrimp gently and stir in lime off the heat. Robert Irvine’s separate roux-and-cream version below keeps its full vegetables, cream and garnishes.

## Directions

1. **Roast the corn:** Preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Toss corn kernels, neutral vegetable oil, and salt and black pepper on a rimmed sheet pan and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 15 minutes, stirring as needed, until fragrant with browned edges, without blackening. Use more pans or roasting loads at larger scales. Begin the pot stages while the corn roasts.
2. **Render the bacon:** Use slices of bacon in a roomy heavy-bottomed soup pot over medium heat. Cook until crisp, stirring, then transfer the bacon bits to a plate and leave all rendered fat in the pot.
3. **Soften the onion:** Add red onion to the bacon fat and cook about 5 minutes until softened without burning.
4. **Add garlic and paprika:** Stir in garlic cloves and smoked paprika and cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant; lower the heat if they catch.
5. **Cook the potatoes:** Add Red Bliss potatoes and chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for about 15–20 minutes, until a fork passes easily through the potato pieces. Stir occasionally so the bottom stays clear; the pot needs headroom above the full liquids and vegetables.
6. **Thicken while keeping texture:** Stir in heavy cream and all the roasted corn. Take the pot safely off the heat. With a hot-liquid-rated immersion blender, keep the blade guard submerged, pulse briefly and stop the motor before lifting it; begin with 3–4 short pulses and leave recognizable corn and potato pieces. Return to low heat and bring to a gentle simmer.
7. **Cook the shrimp completely:** Stir in all raw shrimp. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
8. **Finish with lime and bacon:** Turn off the heat and stir in fresh lime juice and all reserved bacon bits. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve promptly while the shrimp remain tender.

## Cooking Notes

For a fresh count-based version of the six-portion chowder, use all kernels from 4 ears instead of the measured 3 cups and scale that ear count with the planned portions; ear size makes its corn density variable. Keep all other main ingredients and method stages the same. The Robert Irvine version below uses its own measured 2 cups corn and eight-portion formula; these are separate complete choices.

## Robert Irvine’s roux-and-cream version

This complete alternative makes 8 planned portions. Choose its ingredient list and method together; at another yield, scale the entire list proportionally. The oil is one ¼ cup total, divided equally between roasting and the pot. The roux, cream, bacon, peppers and garnishes all belong to this version.

- 1 lime, juice and squeezed rind for shrimp marinade; marinade/rind discarded
- 1 lb raw baby shrimp, shelled, deveined and thawed under refrigeration if frozen
- 2 cups corn kernels, fresh or thawed frozen and drained; do not use canned corn
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil, one total, divided equally between corn roasting and the pot
- 1/2 cup raw bacon, chopped
- 1 red onion, diced
- 1/2 cup celery, finely diced
- 1 green bell pepper, diced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 6 garlic cloves, minced
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 cups heavy cream
- 6 cups chicken stock
- 1/2 lb Red Bliss potatoes, diced into similar small pieces
- 3 tbsp fresh lime juice
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley leaves, chopped
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
- 1 bunch of scallions, chopped
- oyster crackers, as an accompaniment

1. **Chill the lime-marinated shrimp:** Use lime and raw baby shrimp: squeeze the lime over the raw shrimp, add the squeezed rind, stir, cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below while preparing the chowder, for no longer than 1 hour. At large scales, start marinating close enough to the shrimp-cooking stage to keep within that hour; keep all waiting raw shrimp refrigerated.
2. **Roast the corn with half the oil:** Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Coat corn kernels and 1/2 of the vegetable oil on a rimmed baking sheet and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 5–10 minutes until fragrant and lightly colored; do not require blackening. Keep the remaining half of the listed oil for the pot.
3. **Cook the bacon with the remaining oil:** Heat 1/2 of the vegetable oil and raw bacon in a heavy-bottomed soup pot over low heat until the bacon is crisp, stirring. Keep all the bacon and fat in the pot.
4. **Soften onion and celery:** Add red onion and celery and cook about 5 minutes without browning.
5. **Add peppers, garlic and corn:** Add green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and garlic cloves and all the roasted corn. Cook another 5 minutes over low heat, stirring without letting the garlic burn.
6. **Cook the flour gently:** Stir in all-purpose flour and cook 6–8 minutes over low heat, stirring so the flour coats the vegetables and does not stick or scorch.
7. **Simmer the creamy base:** Use heavy cream, chicken stock, and Red Bliss potatoes. Stir in the stock gradually to disperse the flour, then add all the cream and potatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 20 minutes, stirring the bottom, until the potatoes are fork-tender. Avoid a hard boil or stuck roux; use a pot with ample working headroom.
8. **Drain and heat the shrimp:** Remove shrimp from the marinade and discard the liquid and lime rind. Add all shrimp with fresh lime juice, fresh parsley leaves, and cayenne pepper to the gently simmering chowder. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
9. **Garnish with scallions:** Spoon the chowder into bowls and add bunch of scallions and oyster crackers. Serve promptly; all the cream, oil, bacon and vegetables belong to this complete version.

Allow roughly 75–120 minutes elapsed with 45–60 minutes active work, starting with thawed shrimp and including up to 1 hour refrigerated marinating. Roast corn and build the pot base while shrimp marinate, keeping within that hour. Use the same shrimp endpoint, cold-storage and reheating guidance as above.

## Chef's Note

Robert Irvine’s corn chowder cooks bacon, celery, peppers and roasted corn into a full flour-and-cream base. The oil is divided between roasting and the pot. Keep lime-marinated shrimp cold, add them only after the potatoes are tender, and heat them completely before finishing with scallions and oyster crackers.

## Directions

1. **Chill the lime-marinated shrimp:** Use lime and raw baby shrimp: squeeze the lime over the raw shrimp, add the squeezed rind, stir, cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below while preparing the chowder, for no longer than 1 hour. At large scales, start marinating close enough to the shrimp-cooking stage to keep within that hour; keep all waiting raw shrimp refrigerated.
2. **Roast the corn with half the oil:** Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Coat corn kernels and 1/2 of the vegetable oil on a rimmed baking sheet and spread in an uncrowded layer. Roast about 5–10 minutes until fragrant and lightly colored; do not require blackening. Keep the remaining half of the listed oil for the pot.
3. **Cook the bacon with the remaining oil:** Heat 1/2 of the vegetable oil and raw bacon in a heavy-bottomed soup pot over low heat until the bacon is crisp, stirring. Keep all the bacon and fat in the pot.
4. **Soften onion and celery:** Add red onion and celery and cook about 5 minutes without browning.
5. **Add peppers, garlic and corn:** Add green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and garlic cloves and all the roasted corn. Cook another 5 minutes over low heat, stirring without letting the garlic burn.
6. **Cook the flour gently:** Stir in all-purpose flour and cook 6–8 minutes over low heat, stirring so the flour coats the vegetables and does not stick or scorch.
7. **Simmer the creamy base:** Use heavy cream, chicken stock, and Red Bliss potatoes. Stir in the stock gradually to disperse the flour, then add all the cream and potatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 20 minutes, stirring the bottom, until the potatoes are fork-tender. Avoid a hard boil or stuck roux; use a pot with ample working headroom.
8. **Drain and heat the shrimp:** Remove shrimp from the marinade and discard the liquid and lime rind. Add all shrimp with fresh lime juice, fresh parsley leaves, and cayenne pepper to the gently simmering chowder. Start checking after 2–3 minutes and continue until the shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout, with thick centers reaching 145°F / 63°C. Size and starting temperature change the cooking time; pink color alone is not the endpoint.
9. **Garnish with scallions:** Spoon the chowder into bowls and add bunch of scallions and oyster crackers. Serve promptly; all the cream, oil, bacon and vegetables belong to this complete version.

## Cooking Notes

This is the separate eight-portion roux-and-cream version. The [saved bacon-and-paprika chowder](/mise/recipes/roasted-corn-chowder-with-lime-cured-shrimp) has a different six-portion formula. Choose either complete recipe rather than combining their corn, cream or oil quantities.
